code_source: lib/prototypes.ts (the constants the live classifier imports)

classifier.method: Five features per face. Each feature is compared to each of the seven shape prototypes in units of its own spread (z = (x - mu) / sigma), weighted, and summed into one distance per shape. The smallest distance wins; the confidence shown on the site is the raw output of that comparison, rounded, never clamped.
classifier.landmark_note: MediaPipe Face Landmarker, 478 points; ten are used: hairline, chin tip, both cheekbones, both forehead edges, both jaw corners, both chin sides. MediaPipe x/y normalisation is undone before measuring.

features.A: angle at the jaw corner, in degrees

scales.note: The detector measures landmark ratios; a tape measure measures different points. The two scales are related by a per-feature affine map (endpoint to endpoint), so z-scores are identical in both and either table is an exact description of the classifier. Numbers shown to users on the site are tape-measure-scale numbers.

weights_note: Between-group / within-group variance ratios normalised to mean 1 on a 50-photo calibration set (oval 18 / oblong 12 / round 10 / square 6 / heart 1 / diamond 3 / triangle 0). C carries no shape signal in that set (ratio < 1) and is damped to 0.49 but never zeroed: weight 0 in the code means the feature could not be measured on that face.
manual_angle_boost_note: A user-measured jaw angle is trusted over an estimated one: the A weight is multiplied by this factor when the user supplies their own measurement. Declared assumption, not a fitted result - the calibration set contains no same-person measured-vs-estimated angle pairs.
disclosed_limitations: heart (n=1), diamond (n=3) and triangle (n=0) prototypes are interpolated along the literature ordering, not measured.

Measured jaw angle does not separate square from round in the calibration set (both group means near 133 degrees), while the literature separates them by 24 degrees. The A ordering follows the literature because the classification system is built on it; this is why the site reports mixed-shape hints and confidence instead of a single answer.
Calibration data: 50 local photographs, MediaPipe GPU inference, single-annotator draft labels.
